title: Debugging a production incident: stop the harm first, then find the cause
captions: An SLO alert pages you. The error rate on checkout has jumped from 0.2% to 6%. Users are failing to pay right now.
Do not hunt for the cause yet. First make users safe: roll back the last deploy, turn off a feature flag, or shed load. Keep some logs and one bad host for later.
Ask what changed just before the errors started. Look at deploys, config and flags, traffic, and the services you depend on.
Pick the most likely explanation and write it down as one hypothesis. A good hypothesis says what you should see if it is true.
Test it. Split the errors by version, region, tenant or time. If the data says no, go back and try the next hypothesis. A clear no is useful too.
The data agrees, and you can explain the whole story. Often it is not one cause but several conditions that met at the same time.
Write a blameless postmortem. Each action, like a validation check or a kill switch, gets an owner and a date, so the same failure is less likely to come back.
